items.q3: بابل د کوم تمدن ښاري دولت و؟ (الف) د سند دره (ب) میزوپوټامیا (ج) مصري (د) شانګ کورنۍ

items.q: Sumerian Civilization developed along:
items.q2: سومیری تہذیب کس دریا کے ساتھ پروان چڑھی؟ (الف) نیل (ب) فرات (ج) دجلہ (د) زرد دریا
items.q3: سومري تمدن د کوم سیند پر غاړه وده وکړه؟ (الف) نیل (ب) فرات (ج) دجله (د) ژیړ سیند
items.e: Sumer lay between the Tigris and Euphrates; most Sumerian cities (Ur, Uruk, Eridu) were on the Euphrates.

items.q: Identify two early river valley Civilizations.
items.q2: دو ابتدائی دریائی وادی کی تہذیبوں کی نشاندہی کریں۔
items.q3: دوه لومړني د سیند درې تمدنونه وښیاست.
items.a: (1) Mesopotamian civilization — along the Tigris and Euphrates; (2) Egyptian civilization — along the Nile. (Others: Indus Valley along the Indus; Chinese along the Yellow River.)

items.q: What was Cuneiform?
items.q2: خطِ میخی کیا تھا؟
items.q3: مېخي لیک څه و؟
items.a: Cuneiform was the earliest form of writing, invented by the Sumerians. It used wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay tablets; Hammurabi's code was also written in cuneiform.
items.e: سومیریوں کی ایجاد کردہ قدیم ترین تحریر، مٹی کی تختیوں پر میخ نما نشانات۔

items.q: Why was Babylonian Civilization important?
items.q2: بابلی تہذیب کیوں اہم تھی؟
items.q3: بابلي تمدن ولې مهم و؟
items.a: The Babylonians were among the first empire builders of Mesopotamia. Under Hammurabi, Babylon became a cradle of learning and culture, with magnificent buildings, royal palaces, gardens and ziggurats; the Hanging Gardens became one of the Seven Wonders. Most importantly, Hammurabi's Code was one of the first written law codes: it protected the weak, promoted morality, punished wrongdoers and introduced the idea that government should compensate victims.
items.e: اولین سلطنت ساز؛ علم و ثقافت کا گہوارہ؛ معلق باغات؛ حمورابی کا تحریری ضابطۂ قانون۔

items.q: Describe the position of women in the ancient civilizations.
items.q2: قدیم تہذیبوں میں عورتوں کا مقام بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په لرغونو تمدنونو کې د ښځو دریځ بیان کړئ.
items.a: Sumer: women had some independence and respect; they ran households, served as priestesses, and some could buy and sell property and slaves, run businesses and perform ceremonies. Egypt: men headed families and wives managed the household and children's education, but women could own and pass on property, run businesses and even become pharaoh (Hatshepsut). In most other early civilizations men had more rights than women.
items.e: سومر: پجارن، جائیداد، کاروبار؛ مصر: جائیداد، کاروبار، فرعون تک (حتشپسوت)۔

items.q: In the Babylonian Empire, the Code of Hammurabi was regarded as extremely important. In your opinion, how important is a system of strong justice for the development of Pakistan?
items.q2: بابلی سلطنت میں حمورابی کے ضابطے کو انتہائی اہم سمجھا جاتا تھا۔ آپ کی رائے میں پاکستان کی ترقی کے لیے مضبوط نظامِ انصاف کتنا اہم ہے؟
items.q3: په بابلي امپراتورۍ کې د حمورابي قانون ډېر مهم ګڼل کېده. ستاسو په نظر د پاکستان د پرمختګ لپاره قوي عدلي نظام څومره مهم دی؟
items.a: Very important. Fair laws applied equally to rich and poor protect people's rights and property, build trust in the government and encourage investment and business. Babylon declined when laws were applied unfairly after Hammurabi; in the same way, quick and fair justice in Pakistan would reduce crime and corruption, protect the weak and help the country develop.
items.e: Open-ended — any reasoned opinion is acceptable.

items.q: What should be the primary goal of laws: to encourage good behaviour or to punish bad behaviour? Do all communities need a system of law?
items.q2: قوانین کا بنیادی مقصد کیا ہو؟ کیا ہر معاشرے کو قانون کی ضرورت ہے؟
items.q3: د قوانینو موخه څه وي؟ ایا ټولې ټولنې قانون ته اړتیا لري؟
items.a: Sample view: laws should do both — guide people towards good behaviour and fairly punish wrongdoing (as Hammurabi's code aimed: protect the weak, uphold morality, punish evil-doers). As civilizations grow, more people live together, trade and own property, so disputes increase; every community needs clear, fairly applied laws to keep order and protect rights.
items.e: Open discussion — any reasoned view is acceptable.

items.q: Study the map and describe the location of the Nile River and other important landmarks of Egypt.
items.q2: نقشے کی مدد سے دریائے نیل اور مصر کے دوسرے اہم مقامات کا محلِ وقوع بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د نقشې په مرسته د نیل او د مصر د نورو مهمو ځایونو موقعیت بیان کړئ.
items.a: The Nile flows from the south (Nubia) northwards through Upper Egypt and fans out into the delta of Lower Egypt before entering the Mediterranean Sea. The Western (Libyan) Desert lies to its west, the Eastern Desert between the Nile and the Red Sea, and the Sinai Peninsula in the north-east.
items.e: Life was concentrated in the narrow fertile strip along the river.

items.q: How useful is the tomb painting as a source for understanding the agricultural activities of ancient Egyptians?
items.q2: مقبرے کی تصویر قدیم مصری زراعت سمجھنے کے لیے کتنی مفید ہے؟
items.q3: د مقبرې انځور د مصري کرنې د پوهېدو لپاره څومره ګټور دی؟
items.a: Quite useful: it was made at the time, so it shows the real tools (plough, seed), animals (oxen) and crops/trees and who did the work (a man ploughing, a woman sowing). But it may be idealised — tomb art showed a perfect life for the afterlife — so it should be checked against other sources such as written records and excavated tools.
items.e: Any reasoned answer weighing usefulness and bias is acceptable.

items.q: Why were the pyramids built, and how do they still affect us today?
items.q2: اہرام کیوں بنائے گئے اور آج بھی ہم پر کیسے اثر انداز ہوتے ہیں؟
items.q3: هرمونه ولې جوړ شول او نن پر موږ څه اغېز لري؟
items.a: They were built as tombs for pharaohs, because Egyptians believed in the afterlife and wanted to protect the king's body and belongings for the next life. Today they teach us about ancient engineering, mathematics, beliefs and daily life; they are World Heritage sites that attract tourists and bring income to Egypt.

items.q: Complete the chart: Opinion — "Pharaohs were always powerful in ancient Egypt." Give facts and historical interpretations.
items.q2: چارٹ مکمل کریں: رائے — ”قدیم مصر میں فرعون ہمیشہ طاقتور تھے“؛ حقائق اور تاریخی تشریحات لکھیں۔
items.q3: چارټ بشپړ کړئ: نظر — "فرعونان تل ځواکمن وو"؛ حقایق او تاریخي تفسیرونه ولیکئ.
items.a: Facts: the pharaoh stood at the top of the social pyramid; all officials reported through the vizier; pharaohs kept Egypt united, issued orders and led religious ceremonies; they commanded armies and had huge pyramids and temples (Giza, Abu Simbel) built by forced labour; farmers paid taxes on their crops. Historical interpretations: Egyptians saw the pharaoh as a god-king, so religion made his power seem divine; control of the Nile's surplus grain and taxes gave wealth; a trained army and loyal priests and scribes kept control.
items.e: Students may also note that power was not always absolute — weak rulers and foreign conquests (Alexander, Rome) show it could be lost.

items.q: Women had rights and they were powerful in the ancient civilization of:
items.q2: کس قدیم تہذیب میں عورتوں کو حقوق حاصل تھے اور وہ طاقتور تھیں؟ (الف) مصر (ب) وادیِ سندھ (ج) شانگ خاندان (د) سومر
items.q3: په کوم لرغوني تمدن کې ښځو حقونه درلودل او ځواکمنې وې؟ (الف) مصر (ب) د سند دره (ج) شانګ کورنۍ (د) سومر
items.e: The text says Egyptian women had rights and freedom and could even become pharaoh (Hatshepsut); it also describes some Sumerian women as powerful, so d. Sumer is arguable.

items.q: UR was an ancient city state in:
items.q2: اُر قدیم شہری ریاست کہاں تھی؟ (الف) مصر (ب) ایران (ج) سومر (د) اناطولیہ
items.q3: اور لرغونی ښاري دولت چېرې و؟ (الف) مصر (ب) ایران (ج) سومر (د) اناتولیا

items.q: What was the method of mummification and why did Egyptians do it?
items.q2: ممی بنانے کا طریقہ کیا تھا اور مصری ایسا کیوں کرتے تھے؟
items.q3: د مومیا جوړولو طریقه څه وه او مصریانو ولې کوله؟
items.a: The body was wrapped in cloth and adorned with jewels and charms; a mask bearing the likeness of the dead person was placed on the face, and drinks, food and riches were buried with the mummy. Egyptians did this because they believed in life after death and wanted the body preserved for the afterlife.
items.e: لاش کو کپڑے میں لپیٹ کر زیورات سے سجایا جاتا، چہرے پر نقاب؛ بعد از موت زندگی کے عقیدے کی وجہ سے۔

items.q: Describe the irrigation methods in ancient Egypt.
items.q2: قدیم مصر میں آب پاشی کے طریقے بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په لرغوني مصر کې د اوبو لګولو طریقې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Egyptians depended on the Nile, which gave water and fertile soil all year round. They widely used the shaduf — a hand-operated device with a long pole, a bucket at one end and a weight at the other — to lift water from the river or canals into their fields. (They also dug canals and basins to hold floodwater.)
items.e: نیل کا پانی؛ شادوف سے پانی اٹھانا؛ نہریں اور حوض۔

items.q: Compare the position of women in Egyptian Civilization with that in modern times. Make a list of points and share with the class.
items.q2: مصری تہذیب میں عورتوں کے مقام کا آج کے دور سے موازنہ کریں۔ نکات کی فہرست بنا کر جماعت سے شیئر کریں۔
items.q3: په مصري تمدن کې د ښځو دریځ له نني وخت سره پرتله کړئ؛ د ټکو لېست جوړ او ټولګي ته یې وړاندې کړئ.
items.a: Then: men headed families; women ran the household and children's education; they could own and pass on property, run businesses and occasionally rule (Hatshepsut). Now: women can vote, study at all levels, work in every profession, own property and businesses, and serve as heads of government (e.g. Benazir Bhutto in Pakistan); laws guarantee equal rights, though challenges remain.

items.q: Write down more words that you find difficult in this unit. (Words | Meaning)
items.q2: اس یونٹ میں جو مزید الفاظ مشکل لگیں وہ لکھیں۔ (الفاظ | معنی)
items.q3: په دې یونټ کې نور ستونزمن ټکي ولیکئ. (ټکي | مانا)
items.a: Sample: Pharaoh — king of ancient Egypt; Vizier — chief minister; Shaduf — hand-operated water-lifting device; Mummification — preserving a dead body; Cuneiform — wedge-shaped Sumerian writing.

items.q: What does the portrait tell you about King Wu?
items.q2: یہ تصویر بادشاہ وو کے بارے میں کیا بتاتی ہے؟
items.q3: دا انځور د پاچا وو په اړه څه وايي؟
items.a: Details: a tall, richly decorated crown, fine robes with a broad collar, a calm, serious face and a well-groomed beard. Inference: he was a wealthy, powerful and respected ruler. Message: the artist wanted to show King Wu (founder of the Zhou dynasty) as a dignified, wise and confident leader worthy of power.
items.e: Note that a portrait made later may idealise the ruler.

items.q: Describe the information provided by the map about Chinese civilizations.
items.q2: نقشے میں چینی تہذیبوں کے بارے میں دی گئی معلومات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د چیني تمدنونو په اړه د نقشې معلومات بیان کړئ.
items.a: The map shows that the earliest dynasties grew up in northern China along the Yellow River (Huang He). The Xia occupied a small area around Erlitou and Luoyang; the Shang ruled a larger area around Anyang, Ao and Yin; the Zhou spread much wider, from Hao in the west to the coast and south to the Yangzi River. Each dynasty controlled more land than the one before. The Yellow Sea, East China Sea and South China Sea lie to the east.
items.e: ابتدائی خاندان دریائے زرد کے ساتھ؛ ژیا چھوٹا، شانگ بڑا، ژو سب سے وسیع؛ ہر خاندان پچھلے سے بڑا۔

items.q: Which countries use chopsticks as eating utensils?
items.q2: کون سے ممالک کھانے کے لیے چاپ اسٹکس استعمال کرتے ہیں؟
items.q3: کوم هېوادونه د خوړو لپاره چاپسټیک کاروي؟
items.a: China, Japan, North and South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan and Singapore; they are also used in parts of Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia and Myanmar, mainly for noodle and rice dishes.
items.e: چین، جاپان، کوریا، ویت نام، تائیوان، سنگاپور وغیرہ۔

items.q: Describe the impression the "Town Planning in Mehrgarh" picture gives of Mehrgarh civilization.
items.q2: ”مہرگڑھ میں شہری منصوبہ بندی“ کی تصویر مہرگڑھ کا کیا تاثر دیتی ہے؟
items.q3: "په مهرګړ کې ښاري پلان" انځور د مهرګړ څه اغېز ورکوي؟
items.a: The neat rows of rectangular rooms with straight mud-brick walls show that the people planned their settlement carefully. They lived in permanent houses, probably stored grain in the small compartments, and worked together as an organised community — a settled farming society, not wandering hunters.
items.e: منظم مستطیل کمرے، مٹی کی اینٹوں کی دیواریں — مستقل، منظم زرعی بستی۔

items.q: What can we learn about the Indus civilization from the animal engravings on the seals?
items.q2: مہروں پر جانوروں کی کندہ کاری سے ہم وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کے بارے میں کیا جان سکتے ہیں؟
items.q3: په مهرونو د څارویو له حکاکۍ د سند تمدن په اړه څه زده کوو؟
items.a: The animals (bulls, zebu, elephants, tigers, rhinoceros) show which animals lived in the region and which were kept or valued — humped bulls suggest farming and herding. Some animals may have been sacred or symbols of gods, showing religious beliefs. The fine carving shows skilled craftsmen, and the seals were probably used by traders to stamp and identify goods.

items.q: How close is your city to Mohenjo Daro and Harappa?
items.q2: آپ کا شہر موہنجوداڑو اور ہڑپہ سے کتنا قریب ہے؟
items.q3: ستاسو ښار موهنجوداړو او هړپې ته څومره نږدې دی؟
items.a: Sample (Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa): Harappa (Sahiwal district, Punjab) is about 450 km to the south-east, and Mohenjo-Daro (Larkana district, Sindh) is about 900 km to the south, down the Indus. Both lie in the plains of the Indus river system, while Peshawar lies near its north-western edge.
items.e: Answers depend on the student's own city.

items.q: Add a few more points to the list.
items.q2: فہرست میں چند مزید نکات شامل کریں۔
items.q3: لېست ته څو نور ټکي ورزیات کړئ.
items.a: Sample points: The Xia, Shang, Zhou and Qin dynasties ruled ancient China in turn. The Shang produced writing (oracle bone script), bronze vessels, chariots and an accurate calendar. Mehrgarh (7000–5500 BC) near the Bolan Pass was the forerunner of the Indus Valley Civilization. Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro had planned streets, covered drains, a granary and the Great Bath. The Indus script has not been deciphered, and the end of the civilization around 1750 BC is still a mystery.
items.e: ژیا، شانگ، ژو، چِن؛ شانگ کی ایجادات؛ مہرگڑھ پیش رو؛ منصوبہ بند شہر؛ ناقابلِ فہم رسم الخط اور پراسرار خاتمہ۔

items.q: Chopsticks were invented in:
items.q2: چاپ اسٹکس کہاں ایجاد ہوئیں؟ (الف) چین (ب) سومر (ج) ہڑپہ (د) مہرگڑھ
items.q3: چاپسټیک چېرې اختراع شول؟ (الف) چین (ب) سومر (ج) هړپه (د) مهرګړ

items.q: Why were seals used in ancient civilizations?
items.q2: قدیم تہذیبوں میں مہریں کیوں استعمال ہوتی تھیں؟
items.q3: په لرغونو تمدنونو کې مهرونه ولې کارېدل؟
items.a: Seals were pressed into clay to mark ownership and identify goods in trade, to seal containers and documents, and possibly as religious or official symbols. Sumerian seals found far away show trade with Egypt and the Indus Valley; Indus seals with animals and script were probably used by merchants.
items.e: ملکیت اور تجارتی سامان کی نشاندہی، برتن اور دستاویزات سیل کرنے اور مذہبی علامت کے طور پر۔

items.q: Compare the Shang and Zhou dynasties and Indus valley civilazation in terms of governance and religion.
items.q2: شانگ اور ژو خاندانوں اور وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کا حکمرانی اور مذہب کے لحاظ سے موازنہ کریں۔
items.q3: د شانګ او ژو کورنۍ او د سند تمدن د حکومتولۍ او دین له مخې پرتله کړئ.
items.a: Governance: the Shang were ruled by absolute monarchs and the Zhou by a feudal system in which local lords loyal to the emperor ruled villages; the king alone made laws, and society was a strict hierarchy (emperor, nobles, peasants, artisans, merchants, slaves). In the Indus Valley, governance seems to have been based on religion and trade, with commands from priests or monarchs, laws on caring for nature, avoiding violence and paying taxes, and four classes (priests, warriors, traders, workers). Religion: both were polytheistic; the Shang worshipped the spirits of their ancestors for blessings, while the Indus people's beliefs are known only from seals and figurines with animals and humans. Difference: Chinese rulers are known by name from records, but Indus rulers are unknown because their script is undeciphered.
items.e: شانگ مطلق بادشاہت، ژو جاگیرداری؛ سندھ: مذہب و تجارت پر مبنی، پجاری یا بادشاہ؛ دونوں کثیر خدائی؛ شانگ آبا کی روحوں کی پرستش؛ سندھ کے حکمران نامعلوم۔

items.q: Match each claim with its evidence.
items.q2: ہر دعوے کو اس کے ثبوت سے ملائیں۔
items.q3: هره ادعا له خپل ثبوت سره سمه کړئ.
items.a: Used mud bricks for buildings → houses made of bricks found at Mohenjo Daro. Skilled craftsmen → artifacts such as the stone statue with an ornate headband, toy carts and jewellery. Traded with other people → seals with animal pictures probably used for trading goods. Peaceful → excavations at Mohenjo Daro did not reveal weapons. Domesticated animals → animal footprints in mud, toy animals, animal bones and animal pictures on seals.
items.e: اینٹیں ← مکانات؛ کاریگر ← نوادرات؛ تجارت ← مہریں؛ پرامن ← ہتھیار نہیں؛ جانور پالنا ← پاؤں کے نشان اور ہڈیاں۔

items.q: The majority of countries are made up of various ethnic groups. What, in your opinion, binds these different ethnic groups together into a single national identity? Talk about it in small groups.
items.q2: زیادہ تر ممالک مختلف نسلی گروہوں پر مشتمل ہیں۔ آپ کی رائے میں کون سی چیز ان مختلف گروہوں کو ایک قومی شناخت میں باندھتی ہے؟ چھوٹے گروہوں میں اس پر بات کریں۔
items.q3: ډېری هېوادونه له بېلابېلو قومي ډلو جوړ دي. ستاسو په اند څه شی دا ډلې په یوه ملي هویت کې سره تړي؟ په کوچنیو ډلو کې پرې خبرې وکړئ.
items.a: Shared religion and values, a common history and struggle (e.g. the Pakistan Movement), a national language (Urdu) that everyone can use, the constitution and equal rights under the law, national symbols (flag, anthem, national days), shared culture, sports and festivals, and common goals for the country's future. In Pakistan, Punjabis, Sindhis, Pashtuns, Baloch and others are united by Islam, the national language and love for their country.

items.q: Many modern things were created by ancient Chinese people. Give examples and explain how they are used.
items.q2: قدیم چینیوں کی بنائی ہوئی جدید چیزوں کی مثالیں دیں اور ان کا استعمال بتائیں۔
items.q3: د لرغونو چینیانو د جوړو شوو عصري شیانو بېلګې ورکړئ او کارول یې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Paper (writing and printing), printing (books and newspapers), the compass (navigation), gunpowder (fireworks and mining), silk (cloth), tea (a drink), porcelain/china (dishes), chopsticks (eating), the kite (play and early signalling), the umbrella (protection from rain and sun) and the wheelbarrow (carrying loads).
items.e: Several of these were invented after the Shang and Zhou periods.

items.q: Write down more words and their meanings that you find difficult in this unit. (Words | Meaning)
items.q2: اس یونٹ کے مزید مشکل الفاظ اور ان کے معنی لکھیں۔ (الفاظ | معنی)
items.q3: د دې یونټ نور ستونزمن ټکي او ماناوې یې ولیکئ. (ټکي | مانا)
items.a: Sample: Dynasty — a line of rulers from one family; Feudal — a system in which lords hold land from a king in return for loyalty; Granary — a store for grain; Seal — a stamp pressed into clay to mark goods; Hypothesis — an educated guess that explains an event.

items.q: How did farmers pay for the use of the land they farmed?
items.q2: کسان جس زمین پر کاشت کرتے تھے اس کے استعمال کا معاوضہ کیسے ادا کرتے تھے؟
items.q3: بزګرانو د هغې ځمکې د کارولو بدل څنګه ورکاوه چې کرله یې؟
items.a: The land belonged to local lords who were loyal to the emperor. Farmers paid for using it by giving the lord a share of their crops (grain and rice) and by working for him — farming his fields, building walls and serving as soldiers when needed.
items.e: This follows the feudal system of the Zhou described on the previous page.

items.q: Is Confucius more concerned with personal behaviour or with behaviour towards others? Explain your choice.
items.q2: کیا کنفیوشس ذاتی رویّے سے زیادہ متعلق ہے یا دوسروں کے ساتھ رویّے سے؟
items.q3: ایا کنفیوشس شخصي چلند ته ډېر پام کوي که له نورو سره چلند ته؟
items.a: Mainly behaviour towards others: he taught children to respect elders, leaders to be role models for their people, and justice, respect, love and sincerity in governing. These rules are about how people treat each other in families and society — though they start with good personal behaviour and moral character.
items.e: Either answer is acceptable if explained.

items.q: Enlist the inventions and discoveries made by Shang and Zhou dynasty.
items.q2: شانگ اور ژو خاندانوں کی ایجادات اور دریافتوں کی فہرست بنائیں۔
items.q3: د شانګ او ژو کورنیو اختراعات او موندنې لېست کړئ.
items.a: They studied the movement of the planets, recorded eclipses and developed an accurate calendar. The Shang produced a writing system (oracle bone script), exquisite bronze vessels, horse-drawn chariots and bronze weapons. Chopsticks, foot-pedalled hammers for threshing, walled cities and the beginnings of the Grand Canal are also linked with this period.
items.e: سیاروں کا مطالعہ، گرہن، کیلنڈر؛ تحریر، کانسی کے برتن، رتھ، ہتھیار؛ چاپ اسٹکس۔

items.q: Do you think that the economy of Shang and Zhou dynasty was strong? Explain with the help of evidences given in the chapter.
items.q2: کیا آپ کے خیال میں شانگ اور ژو خاندانوں کی معیشت مضبوط تھی؟ سبق میں دیے گئے شواہد سے وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: ایا ستاسو په اند د شانګ او ژو اقتصاد پیاوړی و؟ د لوست د شواهدو په مرسته یې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Yes. The economy was based on agriculture, and the fertile alluvial soil on both sides of the Yellow River let farmers grow surplus food; rice was grown in large flooded fields, and oxen and water buffalo pulled ploughs and carts. The surplus created wealth and freed skilled labour for great projects — Shang tombs, walled cities and the Grand Canal — and for exquisite bronze vessels, which were a sign of power.
items.e: ہاں: زرخیز رسوبی مٹی، اضافی خوراک، چاول؛ دولت سے مقبرے، فصیل بند شہر، گرینڈ کینال اور کانسی کے برتن۔

items.q: What was the ethical code of Confucius?
items.q2: کنفیوشس کا اخلاقی ضابطہ کیا تھا؟
items.q3: د کنفیوشس اخلاقي اصول څه وو؟
items.a: Confucius (around 500 BC) taught proper personal behaviour: children should respect their elders, and a good leader should have strong moral character and be a role model for his people. He believed that justice, respect, love, wisdom and sincerity are at the heart of good governance. His Code of Ethical Life is a collection of lessons still relevant in China today, such as "I hear and I forget, I see and I remember, I do and I understand."
items.e: بڑوں کا احترام، رہنما بطور اخلاقی نمونہ، انصاف، احترام، محبت، دانائی اور خلوص۔

items.q: Describe the location of the Mehrgarh civilization on the map of Pakistan.
items.q2: پاکستان کے نقشے پر مہرگڑھ کی تہذیب کا محلِ وقوع بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د پاکستان پر نقشه د مهرګړ موقعیت بیان کړئ.
items.a: Mehrgarh lies in Balochistan, in western Pakistan, at the foot of the Bolan Pass on the Kachhi plain (near present-day Sibi), west of the Indus River and south-west of Harappa.
items.e: بلوچستان، درۂ بولان کے دامن میں کچھی کے میدان میں، سبی کے قریب، دریائے سندھ کے مغرب میں۔

items.q: The Mehrgarh people had knowledge about metal technology, as evidenced by:
items.q2: مہرگڑھ کے لوگوں کو دھات کاری کا علم تھا، جس کا ثبوت ہے: (الف) موتی (ب) برتن (ج) سوراخ دار کلہاڑی (د) مہریں
items.q3: د مهرګړ خلکو د فلزي ټکنالوژۍ پوهه درلوده، ثبوت یې دی: (الف) مرغلرې (ب) لوښي (ج) سوري لرونکی تبر (د) مهرونه
items.e: The bronze shaft-hole axe is a metal object.

items.q: Describe the early settlements in Mehergarh.
items.q2: مہرگڑھ کی ابتدائی بستیوں کو بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په مهرګړ کې لومړنۍ مېشتې سیمې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Between 7000 and 5500 BC, Mehrgarh was a small farming and herding village at the foot of the Bolan Pass in Balochistan. People lived in planned mud-brick houses with many rooms, grew crops (including cotton) and kept cattle. Finds such as figurines, polychrome pottery, beads, seals and a shaft-hole axe show a developed society; it is thought to be the forerunner of the Indus Valley Civilization.
items.e: 7000–5500 ق م، درۂ بولان، مٹی کی اینٹوں کے مکان، کاشت اور مویشی، برتن اور موتی، سندھ تہذیب کا پیش رو۔

items.q: Examine the images and explore the evidence that Harappa and Mohenjo Daro were well-planned and well-constructed.
items.q2: تصاویر کی مدد سے ثابت کریں کہ ہڑپہ اور موہنجوداڑو منصوبہ بندی سے بنے تھے۔
items.q3: د انځورونو په مرسته وښیاست چې هړپه او موهنجوداړو پلان شوي وو.
items.a: Straight walls of uniform bricks; streets 10–30 feet wide laid out in a grid; covered drains under the streets leading out of the city; brick-lined wells; and large public buildings such as the Great Bath (with steps and a waterproof lining) and the granary. These show careful planning, skilled builders and a strong local authority.
items.e: یکساں اینٹیں، جال نما چوڑی گلیاں، ڈھکی نالیاں، کنویں، بڑا حمام اور غلہ گودام۔

items.q: Complete the chart (Cities, Trade, Language) and write one conclusion about the Indus Valley civilization.
items.q2: چارٹ (شہر، تجارت، زبان) مکمل کریں اور وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کے بارے میں ایک نتیجہ لکھیں۔
items.q3: چارټ (ښارونه، سوداګري، ژبه) بشپړ کړئ او د سند تمدن په اړه یوه پایله ولیکئ.
items.a: Cities — well-planned cities (Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro) with grid streets 10–30 feet wide, covered drains, a granary and the Great Bath. Trade — farming surplus (cotton, wheat, barley) and crafts were traded; the Indus River eased shipment; seals were used to mark goods. Language — they had a script found on seals, but it has not been deciphered. Conclusion: the Indus Valley was an advanced, organised urban civilization, though much about it is still unknown because we cannot read its writing.
items.e: شہر: منصوبہ بند، نالیاں، حمام؛ تجارت: دریا، مہریں؛ زبان: رسم الخط ناقابلِ فہم؛ نتیجہ: ترقی یافتہ منظم شہری تہذیب۔

items.q: Is evidence such as granaries, public baths and town planning sufficient to prove that the Indus Valley had an advanced civilization?
items.q2: کیا غلہ گودام، عوامی حمام اور شہری منصوبہ بندی ترقی یافتہ تہذیب ثابت کرنے کے لیے کافی ہیں؟
items.q3: ایا ګودامونه، حمامونه او ښاري پلان د پرمختللي تمدن لپاره بس ثبوت دي؟
items.a: Largely yes: building them needed planning, many skilled workers, standard bricks, engineering knowledge (drains, waterproofing) and an authority to organise food storage and public works. But it is not complete proof on its own — we also need other evidence such as seals, writing, trade goods, crafts and art, and since the script cannot be read we cannot know their laws or ideas for certain.
items.e: Reasoned views either way are acceptable.

items.q: Use the clues to build a hypothesis about the end of the Indus Valley Civilization and say what extra information you need to test it.
items.q2: اشاروں کی مدد سے وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کے خاتمے کے بارے میں مفروضہ بنائیں اور بتائیں کہ اسے پرکھنے کے لیے کیا مزید معلومات درکار ہیں۔
items.q3: د نښو په مرسته د سند تمدن د پای په اړه فرضیه جوړه کړئ او ووایاست چې د ازموینې لپاره نور کوم معلومات پکار دي.
items.a: Hypothesis: from about 1750 BC, changes in climate and river courses (drought, floods, the drying of rivers) ruined crops and trade, so the cities slowly declined and people moved away; the weakened cities may then have been attacked, which could explain the unburied skeletons. Extra information needed: dated evidence of climate and river changes (soil and lake studies), the exact dates of the skeletons, signs of burning or weapons, and sources on the arrival of the Aryans (e.g. "Aryan Invasions of India") to see whether they came before or after the decline.

items.q: The Harappan used to store surplus food in:
items.q2: ہڑپہ والے اضافی خوراک کہاں ذخیرہ کرتے تھے؟ (الف) غلہ گودام (ب) سرنگیں (ج) کھیت (د) مکانات
items.q3: هړپه والو اضافي خواړه چېرې ساتل؟ (الف) ګودام (ب) تونلونه (ج) کروندې (د) کورونه

items.q: The settlements in Indus valley were mostly located in:
items.q2: وادیِ سندھ کی بستیاں زیادہ تر کہاں واقع تھیں؟ (الف) جنگلات (ب) کچی آبادیاں (ج) غار (د) شہری علاقے
items.q3: د سند درې مېشتې سیمې ډېری چېرې وې؟ (الف) ځنګلونه (ب) کچه سیمې (ج) سمڅې (د) ښاري سیمې

items.q: Social amusements of Indus people included:
items.q2: سندھی لوگوں کی تفریحات میں شامل تھا: (الف) شکار (ب) تیر اندازی (ج) پانسہ (د) دوڑ
items.q3: د سند خلکو ساتېري کې شامل و: (الف) ښکار (ب) غشي ویشتل (ج) ډایس (د) منډې

items.q: What was the layout of Harappa's town?
items.q2: ہڑپہ کے شہر کا نقشہ کیسا تھا؟
items.q3: د هړپې ښار نقشه څنګه وه؟
items.a: Harappa was a well-planned city. Houses were built of bricks along straight streets 10–30 feet wide laid out in a grid. Small covered drains under the streets carried waste to large drains outside the city. A raised area held important public buildings such as the granary, while the wealthy had houses with large courtyards.
items.e: جال نما چوڑی گلیاں، اینٹوں کے مکان، ڈھکی نالیاں، غلہ گودام، صحن والے مکان۔

items.q: Name some of the primary occupations and lifestyle of the Harappan people.
items.q2: ہڑپہ کے لوگوں کے چند اہم پیشے اور طرزِ زندگی بتائیں۔
items.q3: د هړپه خلکو ځینې اصلي مسلکونه او د ژوند طرز وښیاست.
items.a: Occupations: farming (cotton, wheat, barley, peas, fruits), trade, arts and crafts; potters, masons and metalworkers were in high demand. Lifestyle: they lived in planned cities with drains; men and women wore a dhoti and a shawl; they enjoyed clay modelling and dicing; children played with animal-shaped clay toys; the wealthy had houses with large courtyards.
items.e: کاشتکاری، تجارت، دستکاری، کمہار، معمار، دھات کار؛ دھوتی و شال، پانسہ، مٹی کے کھلونے۔

items.q: Ask the students to summarize what they have learned about the decline or end of the Indus Valley Civilization in this course. They can summarize their ideas by saying something like, "I've learned that there are various theories to explain the demise of the Indus Valley civilization." Information may be presented on a chart paper.
items.q2: طلبہ سے کہیں کہ وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کے زوال یا خاتمے کے بارے میں جو سیکھا اس کا خلاصہ کریں، مثلاً: ”میں نے سیکھا کہ وادیِ سندھ کی تہذیب کے خاتمے کی وضاحت کے لیے کئی نظریات ہیں۔“ معلومات چارٹ پیپر پر پیش کی جا سکتی ہیں۔
items.q3: زده کوونکي دې د سند تمدن د زوال یا پای په اړه خپل زده کړي لنډ کړي، لکه: "ما زده کړل چې د سند تمدن د پای د تشریح لپاره بېلابېلې نظریې شته." معلومات په چارټ کاغذ وړاندې کېدای شي.
items.a: "I've learned that there are various theories to explain the demise of the Indus Valley civilization: (1) natural disasters such as a major drought or flood; (2) the Indus Basin drying up because rivers changed their routes, shortening the rainy season and destroying forests and crops; (3) an attack by enemies, suggested by unburied skeletons at Mohenjo-Daro; (4) the arrival of the Aryans from Central Asia around the same time. Building quality declined from about 1750 BC and the cities slowly decayed, but the true cause is still unknown."
items.e: قدرتی آفات، دریاؤں کے راستے کی تبدیلی، دشمن کا حملہ، آریاؤں کی آمد — اصل وجہ نامعلوم۔

items.q: Which bodies of water surrounded the Empire?
items.q2: سلطنت کے گرد کون سے آبی ذخائر تھے؟
items.q3: امپراتوري کومو اوبو را ګېره کړې وه؟
items.a: The Black Sea, the Caspian Sea, the Mediterranean Sea, the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf and the Arabian Sea (and the Aral Sea in the north-east).
items.e: بحیرۂ اسود، کیسپین، بحیرۂ روم، بحیرۂ احمر، خلیجِ فارس، بحیرۂ عرب۔

items.q: What does the Palace of Cyrus tell you about the Persian Empire?
items.q2: قصرِ سائرس ایرانی سلطنت کے بارے میں کیا بتاتا ہے؟
items.q3: د کوروش ماڼۍ د پارسي امپراتورۍ په اړه څه وايي؟
items.a: The long rows of tall stone columns show a huge, carefully planned building that needed skilled architects, many workers and great wealth. This tells us the empire was rich, powerful and well organised, and that its kings wanted to display their greatness. Its survival for over 2,500 years shows strong building skills.

items.q: Do you see any connections between these Greek inventions and the present world?
items.q2: کیا آپ ان یونانی ایجادات اور آج کی دنیا میں کوئی تعلق دیکھتے ہیں؟
items.q3: ایا د دې یوناني اختراعاتو او نننۍ نړۍ ترمنځ اړیکه وینئ؟
items.a: Yes. Open-air theatres like Epidaurus are copied in modern stadiums and amphitheatres; the Archimedean screw is still used to lift water, grain and sewage; Greek methods of measuring the Earth and studying the Sun and planets led to modern astronomy and space science; and Greek vase shapes and patterns still appear in pottery and design.
items.e: تھیٹر/اسٹیڈیم، ارشمیدسی پیچ آج بھی، فلکیات کی بنیاد، برتنوں کے ڈیزائن۔

items.q: Can you spot designs on the Greek vase that are used in today's objects? Name some everyday items with such patterns.
items.q2: کیا یونانی گلدان کے ڈیزائن آج کی اشیا میں نظر آتے ہیں؟ ایسے نقش والی چند اشیا کے نام بتائیں۔
items.q3: ایا د یوناني ګلدان ډیزاینونه په نننیو شیانو کې لیدل کېږي؟ داسې شیان ونومئ.
items.a: Yes — the vase's shape with two handles, its bands of repeating geometric patterns (such as the "Greek key" or meander) and figure scenes are still used. Such patterns appear on flower vases and mugs, plates and crockery, tiles and borders of carpets, building columns and railings, fabric and clothing borders, and company logos.
items.e: دو دستے، جیومیٹریائی پٹیاں (یونانی کلید)؛ گلدان، برتن، ٹائلیں، قالین، کپڑوں کے کنارے۔

items.q: How did the Indo-Greek kingdoms help the exchange of ideas between East and West?
items.q2: ہند-یونانی سلطنتوں نے مشرق و مغرب کے درمیان خیالات کے تبادلے میں کیسے مدد کی؟
items.q3: هندو-یوناني پاچاهیو د ختیځ او لوېدیځ ترمنځ د مفکورو په تبادله کې څنګه مرسته وکړه؟
items.a: Greek rulers settled in Gandhara and Taxila (e.g. the city of Sirkap), bringing Greek language, coins, town planning and art. Traders and travellers moved along the routes between the Mediterranean, Persia, Central Asia and India. Greek styles of sculpture mixed with local Buddhist and Indus ideas, as seen in Gandhara statues of the Buddha with Greek-style robes and faces, and Indian ideas and goods travelled west.
items.e: یونانی حکمران، سکے، شہری منصوبہ بندی؛ تجارتی راستے؛ گندھارا مجسمے — یونانی انداز اور مقامی بدھ خیالات کا امتزاج۔

items.q: What is Lok Virsa and what is its role in promoting Gandhara art and culture?
items.q2: لوک ورثہ کیا ہے اور گندھارا فن و ثقافت کے فروغ میں اس کا کیا کردار ہے؟
items.q3: لوک ورثه څه دی او د ګندهارا هنر او کلتور په ودې کې یې څه رول دی؟
items.a: Lok Virsa (the National Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage) in Islamabad runs the Heritage Museum, which displays Gandhara sculptures, relics and models of ancient life; it holds exhibitions, festivals and craft programmes, publishes research and helps people learn about and value Pakistan's ancient heritage.
items.e: اسلام آباد کا قومی ادارۂ لوک ورثہ — ہیریٹیج میوزیم، نمائشیں، میلے اور تحقیق۔

items.q: Identify the main areas where Christianity spread, and where it was most widespread by 325 AD.
items.q2: نقشے پر وہ اہم علاقے بتائیں جہاں مسیحیت پھیلی اور 325ء تک کہاں سب سے زیادہ پھیلی۔
items.q3: پر نقشه هغه سیمې وښیاست چې مسیحیت پکې خپور شو او تر 325 ز پورې تر ټولو ډېر چېرې و.
items.a: It spread all around the Mediterranean: Palestine/Judea, Syria, Asia Minor (Turkey), Greece and the Balkans, Egypt and North Africa (Carthage), Italy (Rome), Spain, Gaul (France) and Britain. By 325 AD it was most widespread in the eastern Mediterranean — Asia Minor, Syria, Egypt and Greece — and in North Africa around Carthage.
items.e: بحیرۂ روم کے گرد؛ 325ء تک سب سے زیادہ ایشیائے کوچک، شام، مصر، یونان اور شمالی افریقہ میں۔

items.q: What was similar in the Persian and Greek civilizations?
items.q2: ایرانی اور یونانی تہذیبوں میں کیا مماثلت تھی؟
items.q3: د پارسي او یوناني تمدنونو ترمنځ څه ورته والی و؟
items.a: Both had organised societies divided into classes with slaves at the bottom; both developed fine art and architecture (Persepolis, the Parthenon); both traded widely by land and sea and used metal coins; both had strong armies; and in both, some women could own property and enjoy some freedom.
items.e: طبقاتی معاشرہ، شاندار فنِ تعمیر، وسیع تجارت اور سکے، مضبوط فوج۔

items.q: Describe the main achievements of Greeks in arts, architecture and science.
items.q2: فنون، فنِ تعمیر اور سائنس میں یونانیوں کی اہم کامیابیاں بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په هنرونو، معمارۍ او ساینس کې د یونانیانو اصلي لاسته راوړنې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Arts: beautiful painted vases with figure scenes and geometric patterns, sculpture, drama in open-air theatres such as Epidaurus, and the Olympic Games (776 BC). Architecture: the Acropolis and the Parthenon in Athens (begun 447 BC), temples with columns, and theatres built into hillsides. Science and learning: Eratosthenes estimated the Earth's circumference; Aristarchus estimated the size of the Sun; Ptolemy described a model of the universe; the Archimedean screw lifted water; philosophers such as Socrates (Socratic method), Plato (Academy) and Aristotle (Lyceum) laid foundations of Western thought; and Athens developed democracy.
items.e: فنون: گلدان، مجسمے، تھیٹر، اولمپکس؛ تعمیر: پارتھینن، ایکروپولس؛ سائنس: اراتوستھینز، ارسٹارکس، بطلیموس، ارشمیدسی پیچ، سقراط، افلاطون، ارسطو۔

items.q: Which is more important in measuring effective leadership — election results or integrity? Does a leader have to be popular to succeed?
items.q2: مؤثر قیادت میں کیا زیادہ اہم ہے — انتخابی نتائج یا دیانت داری؟ کیا رہنما کا مقبول ہونا ضروری ہے؟
items.q3: په اغېزناکه مشرۍ کې څه مهم دي — د ټاکنو پایلې که صداقت؟ ایا مشر باید محبوب وي؟
items.a: Sample view: integrity matters more over time — election results show popularity at one moment, but honesty, fairness and keeping promises earn lasting trust. A leader does not have to be popular all the time; good leaders sometimes take unpopular but necessary decisions. Examples: Alexander succeeded through courage, planning and respecting enemies like Porus, but failed when he ignored his tired soldiers; Darius I succeeded by organising the empire (Royal Road, coins), while Darius III failed to defend it. In our country, honest, educated and fair leaders help development, while corruption holds it back.

items.q: Forming opinions: In your opinion, why was it important for the Romans to obey the pope? Also compare this with the outlook of modern Christian world towards Pope.
items.q2: رائے بنانا: آپ کی رائے میں رومیوں کے لیے پوپ کی اطاعت کیوں اہم تھی؟ اس کا موازنہ آج کی مسیحی دنیا کے پوپ کے بارے میں نقطۂ نظر سے کریں۔
items.q3: نظر جوړول: ستاسو په اند رومیانو ته د پاپ اطاعت ولې مهم و؟ دا له نني مسیحي نړۍ د پاپ په اړه لید سره پرتله کړئ.
items.a: Once Rome became the centre of Christianity, the pope (the bishop of Rome) was seen as the leader of the Church, so obeying him meant following religious guidance and kept believers united; his support also gave rulers authority. Today, Catholic Christians still respect the pope as their spiritual leader, but his role is religious and moral rather than political, and many other Christian churches (Protestant, Orthodox) do not follow him.
items.e: The unit does not discuss the pope directly; reasoned opinions are acceptable.

items.q: Identifying Effects: How would a ruler use the Royal Road to keep power in the empire?
items.q2: اثرات کی نشاندہی: ایک حکمران سلطنت میں اقتدار برقرار رکھنے کے لیے شاہراہِ شاہی کو کیسے استعمال کرتا؟
items.q3: اغېزې پېژندل: یو واکمن به د امپراتورۍ د ساتلو لپاره شاهي لار څنګه کاروله؟
items.a: He could send orders and receive news quickly through the postal relay stations; move soldiers fast to stop rebellions or defend borders; collect taxes and tribute from distant provinces; and encourage trade that brought wealth to the empire.
items.e: فوری احکامات اور خبریں، فوج کی تیز نقل و حرکت، ٹیکس کی وصولی، تجارت۔

items.q: Comparing: What modern communication and transportation systems can be compared to the Persians' Royal Road?
items.q2: موازنہ: کون سے جدید مواصلاتی اور نقل و حمل کے نظام ایرانیوں کی شاہراہِ شاہی سے ملتے ہیں؟
items.q3: پرتله: کوم عصري مخابراتي او ترانسپورټي سیسټمونه د پارسیانو له شاهي لارې سره پرتله کېدای شي؟
items.a: Motorways and highways (e.g. Pakistan's motorways, the Karakoram Highway and CPEC routes), railways, postal and courier services, and modern telecommunications — telephone, mobile networks and the internet — which, like the Royal Road, connect distant places and carry goods and messages quickly.
items.e: موٹرویز، شاہراہِ قراقرم، ریلوے، ڈاک و کوریئر، فون اور انٹرنیٹ۔

items.q: What are some historical facts about Hagia Sophia?
items.q2: آیا صوفیہ کے بارے میں چند تاریخی حقائق کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د ایا صوفیې په اړه ځینې تاریخي حقایق څه دي؟
items.a: It was built as a cathedral by the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) emperor Justinian I and completed in AD 537 in Constantinople; its huge dome was an engineering wonder. After Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 it became a mosque, and minarets were added. In 1934 it was made a museum, and in 2020 it was turned back into a mosque. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage "Historic Areas of Istanbul".
items.e: جسٹینین اول نے 537ء میں کلیسا بنایا؛ 1453ء میں مسجد؛ 1934ء میں عجائب گھر؛ 2020ء میں دوبارہ مسجد۔

items.q: Cyrus the Great was emperor of:
items.q2: سائرسِ اعظم کس کا شہنشاہ تھا؟ (الف) وادیِ سندھ (ب) مصر (ج) میسوپوٹیمیا (د) فارس
items.q3: کوروش کبیر د کوم ځای امپراتور و؟ (الف) د سند دره (ب) مصر (ج) میزوپوټامیا (د) پارس

items.q: Which two cities serve as the ending part of the Royal road?
items.q2: کون سے دو شہر شاہراہِ شاہی کے سرے تھے؟
items.q3: کوم دوه ښارونه د شاهي لارې پایونه وو؟
items.a: Sardis in Anatolia (Lydia) and Susa in Persia.

items.q: Which countries were conquered by the Persian Empire? Point out the location with reference to the Subcontinent, especially Pakistan.
items.q2: ایرانی سلطنت نے کون سے ممالک فتح کیے؟ پاکستان کے حوالے سے محلِ وقوع بتائیں۔
items.q3: پارسي امپراتورۍ کوم هېوادونه ونیول؟ د پاکستان په پرتله یې موقعیت وښیاست.
items.a: Lands in today's Turkey (Anatolia, Lydia), Armenia, Thrace and Macedonia (parts of Greece and Bulgaria), Iraq (Babylonia), Syria, Lebanon, Israel/Palestine, Jordan, Egypt and Libya, the Caucasus, Central Asia and Afghanistan. In the east the empire reached the Indus — the Gandhara region and the Indus valley in today's north-western Pakistan were Persian provinces under Darius. So the empire lay to the west and north-west of the Subcontinent and touched Pakistan's western borderlands.
items.e: ترکی، آرمینیا، یونان کے حصے، عراق، شام، مصر، افغانستان، وسطی ایشیا؛ مشرق میں دریائے سندھ تک — گندھارا اور شمال مغربی پاکستان۔

items.q: Use the diagram to identify the similarities and differences between Cyrus and Darius. Which difference do you consider most important and why?
items.q2: خاکے کی مدد سے سائرس اور دارا کی مماثلتیں اور فرق بتائیں۔ کون سا فرق سب سے اہم ہے اور کیوں؟
items.q3: د ډیاګرام په مرسته د کوروش او داریوش ورته والي او توپیرونه وښیاست. کوم توپیر تر ټولو مهم دی او ولې؟
items.a: Cyrus only: founded the Persian Empire and the Achaemenid dynasty; conquered Lydia and Babylon; followed the laws of the lands he conquered. Both: great Achaemenid rulers and warriors; built roads and set up a postal service; tolerant of other religions; brought peace and economic development. Darius only: took the throne after defeating Bardiya; built the Royal Road from Susa to Sardis; promoted learning, agriculture and afforestation; fought the Persian wars with the Greeks. Most important difference (sample): Cyrus created the empire by conquest, while Darius organised it with roads and services so it could be ruled — without his organisation the empire might not have lasted.

items.q: During Persian Empire 'Susa to Sardis' was an early form of:
items.q2: ایرانی سلطنت میں ’سوسا سے سارڈیس‘ کس کی ابتدائی شکل تھی؟ (الف) نہرِ سویز (ب) اسکندریہ (ج) شاہراہِ ریشم (د) قشقائی قالین
items.q3: په پارسي امپراتورۍ کې "له سوسا تر سارډیس" د څه لومړنۍ بڼه وه؟ (الف) سویز کانال (ب) اسکندریه (ج) د ورېښمو لار (د) قشقايي غالۍ
items.e: Susa–Sardis was the Royal Road, a long trade and communication route — the option closest to a road like the later Silk Road.

items.q: What was the origin of Persians?
items.q2: ایرانیوں کی اصل کیا تھی؟
items.q3: د پارسیانو اصل څه و؟
items.a: The Persians belonged to the people group known as the Aryans. They lived in ancient Iran (Persia), a region of south-western Asia, and called their homeland Parsa. The Medes ruled over them until Cyrus the Great (559–530 BC) united them and founded the Achaemenid Empire.
items.e: آریائی نسل؛ قدیم ایران (پارسا)؛ مادیوں کے ماتحت، پھر سائرس نے ہخامنشی سلطنت قائم کی۔

items.q: Describe the importance of the historical city of Taxila.
items.q2: تاریخی شہر ٹیکسلا کی اہمیت بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د ټکسیلا تاریخي ښار اهمیت بیان کړئ.
items.a: Taxila, in Rawalpindi district, was a well-developed city under the Persian Empire. Under Darius I it linked the Gandhara region with the Western world through trade. Caravans brought artistic and cultural influences from many regions, and later the Greek city of Sirkap was built there. It became a centre of Gandhara art and learning, and its ruins are a major archaeological site today.
items.e: فارسی دور میں ترقی یافتہ، گندھارا کا مغرب سے تجارتی رابطہ، سرکپ، گندھارا فن اور علم کا مرکز۔

items.q: Cyrus the Great
items.q2: سائرسِ اعظم
items.q3: کوروش کبیر
items.a: Cyrus the Great (ruled 559–530 BC) founded the Persian (Achaemenid) Empire. An outstanding diplomat and warrior, he won over the Median army, conquered Lydia (550 BC) and Babylon (539 BC) and built one of the world's largest empires. He followed the laws of the lands he conquered and was tolerant of other cultures, which kept his power and preserved those cultures. Roads and a postal service were developed under him and Darius. His tomb stands at Pasargadae in Iran.
items.e: ہخامنشی سلطنت کا بانی، لیڈیا و بابل فتح، روادار، پاسارگاد میں مقبرہ۔

items.q: Describe the places of ancient Greece where Greek civilization developed.
items.q2: قدیم یونان کے وہ مقامات بیان کریں جہاں یونانی تہذیب نے ترقی کی۔
items.q3: د لرغوني یونان هغه ځایونه بیان کړئ چې یوناني تمدن پکې وده وکړه.
items.a: Greek civilization developed on the Balkan Peninsula — Macedonia in the north, central Greece (Delphi, Thebes, Athens) and the Peloponnesus in the south (Corinth, Mycenae, Sparta) — on the island of Crete (Knossos, home of the Minoans), on the many islands of the Aegean Sea, and along the western coast of Asia Minor (present-day Turkey). These lands are mountainous and surrounded by the Ionian, Aegean and Mediterranean Seas, so the Greeks lived in separate city-states and became sailors and traders.
items.e: جزیرہ نمائے بلقان (مقدونیہ، ایتھنز، سپارٹا)، کریٹ، بحیرۂ ایجیئن کے جزائر اور ایشیائے کوچک کا ساحل۔

items.q: How might the ability to own weapons change the attitude of ordinary Greek citizens?
items.q2: ہتھیار رکھنے کی صلاحیت عام یونانی شہریوں کے رویّے کو کیسے بدل سکتی ہے؟
items.q3: د وسلې لرل به د عادي یوناني وګړو چلند څنګه بدل کړي؟
items.a: Citizens who could arm themselves and fight as soldiers felt more important and confident; since the city depended on them for defence, they demanded a greater say in government, which helped the growth of democracy. It could also make society more warlike and encourage conflict between city-states.
items.e: اعتماد اور حکومت میں حصے کا مطالبہ، جمہوریت کی ترقی؛ مگر جنگجوئی بھی بڑھ سکتی تھی۔

items.q: Did Alexander merit the title "Great"? Explain with evidence.
items.q2: کیا سکندر ”اعظم“ کے لقب کا مستحق تھا؟ شواہد سے وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: ایا سکندر د "اعظم" لقب وړ و؟ په شواهدو یې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Yes: by about 30 years of age he had conquered Greece, Persia, Syria, Egypt and lands up to the Punjab; he founded cities such as Alexandria in Egypt and Bucephala on the Jhelum; he respected brave enemies such as Porus; and his conquests spread Greek language and culture (the Hellenistic Age, Gandhara art). No: his wars killed very many people and destroyed cities, his empire broke apart soon after his death in 323 BC, and his own soldiers refused to go further.
items.e: Either opinion is acceptable if backed by evidence.

items.q3: سکندر په لرغوني ____ کې اسکندریه جوړه کړه چې د بطلیموسي پاچاهۍ پلازمېنه شوه: (الف) یونان (ب) مصر (ج) ایران (د) هند

items.q: How was the social and political life in Athens different from Sparta?
items.q2: ایتھنز کی سماجی اور سیاسی زندگی سپارٹا سے کیسے مختلف تھی؟
items.q3: په اتن کې ټولنیز او سیاسي ژوند له سپارټا څنګه توپیر درلود؟
items.a: Athens: a democracy where citizens voted on important decisions such as war; officials were chosen by lottery; it was a centre of philosophy, arts, science and learning (Plato's Academy, Aristotle's Lyceum); it had a small army; formal schooling was mostly for boys from rich families; its golden age came under Pericles. Sparta: a warrior society focused on duty, strength and discipline; its assembly was made up of Spartans; slaves did all manual work so men could train for war; women were educated, did athletics and had more freedom than in other Greek states; the economy relied on agriculture and conquest.
items.e: ایتھنز: جمہوریت، علم و فن، چھوٹی فوج؛ سپارٹا: جنگجو معاشرہ، نظم و ضبط، غلام مشقت کرتے، عورتوں کو زیادہ آزادی۔

items.q: Highlight some of the impacts of Greek Civilization on the Subcontinent.
items.q2: برصغیر پر یونانی تہذیب کے چند اثرات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: پر نیمه وچه د یوناني تمدن ځینې اغېزې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Alexander's conquest spread Greek language, culture and ideas; he founded the cities of Nicaea and Bucephala on the Jhelum; Greek cities such as Sirkap were built at Taxila; East–West exchange grew through Indo-Greek kingdoms; Greek, Indus, Chinese and Persian ideas combined to create the Gandhara School of art; and the weakening of local tribes helped the rise of the Mauryan Empire.
items.e: یونانی زبان و ثقافت، نئے شہر، سرکپ، گندھارا فن، موریہ سلطنت کا عروج۔

items.q: Who was Alexander the Great? Describe his encounter with Raja Porus.
items.q2: سکندرِ اعظم کون تھا؟ راجہ پورس سے اس کے مقابلے کو بیان کریں۔
items.q3: سکندر اعظم څوک و؟ له راجا پورس سره د هغه مخامخ کېدل بیان کړئ.
items.a: Alexander III of Macedon became king in 336 BC and conquered Greece, Persia, Syria and Egypt, where he founded Alexandria (332 BC). Inspired by Greek accounts of India, he advanced into the Punjab, where many tribes surrendered. King Porus, who ruled between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers and had a very brave army with war elephants, refused to accept Alexander's power and fought him. According to the book, Porus resisted successfully and the battle remained indecisive; Alexander, amazed by his courage, made peace and returned his kingdom to him. Alexander wanted to go further east, but his tired soldiers refused, so he turned back.
items.e: مقدونیہ کا بادشاہ (336 ق م)؛ فارس، مصر فتح؛ پنجاب میں پورس سے جنگ؛ پورس کی بہادری، سلطنت واپس؛ سپاہیوں کا آگے جانے سے انکار۔

items.q3: د یوناني تمدن له زوال وروسته رومي امپراتوري د خپل پیاوړي ____ له امله بې سیاله ځواک شوه: (الف) اقتصاد (ب) پوځ (ج) کلتور (د) ډیموکراسي
items.e: The text says "overwhelming military, technological innovation, and vast infrastructure".

items.q: Explain the impact of Christianity on social, religious and political life of people?
items.q2: لوگوں کی سماجی، مذہبی اور سیاسی زندگی پر مسیحیت کے اثرات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د خلکو پر ټولنیز، دیني او سیاسي ژوند د مسیحیت اغېزې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Religious: Christianity became a major world religion, spreading around the Mediterranean to Egypt, North Africa, Syria, Turkey and Greece, and Rome became its centre. Social: Jesus's teachings of peace, forgiveness, love and equality encouraged care for the poor and the family. Political: once the Roman emperors (from Constantine, AD 325) supported Christianity, the Church and its leaders, including the pope in Rome, gained great influence over rulers and laws.
items.e: مذہبی: عالمی مذہب، روم مرکز؛ سماجی: امن، معافی، محبت، مساوات؛ سیاسی: کلیسا اور پوپ کا اثر۔

items.q: Roman Empire
items.q2: رومی سلطنت
items.q3: رومي امپراتوري
items.a: After the decline of Greek civilization, the Roman Empire became the unrivalled power of the known world through its strong military, technology and infrastructure. At its height it stretched from Britain and Spain to Egypt and Asia Minor around the Mediterranean. The Pax Romana (Roman Peace) was its golden age, with a standard currency, a civil service, good roads, a unified legal system and flourishing arts and architecture. Romans built arches, aqueducts, sewers, roads and grid-planned cities and used Roman numerals and the Julian calendar. Christianity rose as a world religion during the empire, and Rome became its centre.
items.e: بے مثال طاقت، پیکس رومانا، کرنسی، سڑکیں، قانون، محرابیں و آبی گزرگاہیں، مسیحیت کا عروج۔

items.q: Describe the routes the Aryans took from the Caucasus Mountains to the Indus Valley, naming physical features along the way.
items.q2: آریاؤں کے کوہِ قفقاز سے وادیِ سندھ تک کے راستے بیان کریں اور راستے کے طبعی خدوخال کے نام بتائیں۔
items.q3: د آریایانو لارې له قفقاز تر سند درې بیان کړئ او د لارې طبیعي ځانګړتیاوې ونومئ.
items.a: From the Caucasus Mountains between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea, one route went north and east around the Caspian Sea, past the Aral Sea, and then south through the mountain passes of the Hindu Kush into the Indus Valley. Another route went south of the Caspian Sea across the Plateau of Iran to the Indus Valley. The Himalayas and the Plateau of Tibet lie to the east of the valley, and the Arabian Sea to the south.
items.e: قفقاز سے کیسپین کے شمال میں ارال کے قریب سے ہندوکش کے راستے؛ یا کیسپین کے جنوب میں سطح مرتفع ایران سے وادیِ سندھ۔

items.q: How can we promote and protect human rights in our country? Explain the likely impact on communities.
items.q2: ہم اپنے ملک میں انسانی حقوق کو کیسے فروغ اور تحفظ دے سکتے ہیں؟ معاشرے پر اثر بتائیں۔
items.q3: موږ په خپل هېواد کې بشري حقونه څنګه هڅولای او ساتلای شو؟ پر ټولنو یې اغېز ووایاست.
items.a: Treat everyone equally regardless of caste, religion, gender or wealth; enforce laws against discrimination and child labour; give free education and health care to all; teach children about rights and respect in schools; build a safety culture (safe workplaces, safe roads, protection for women and children); and help people report abuse to police and courts. Impact: communities become fairer and more peaceful, people trust each other and the government, and more people can study, work and contribute to development.

items.q: What common practices and values are shared by different religions?
items.q2: مختلف مذاہب میں کون سے مشترکہ اعمال اور اقدار ہیں؟
items.q3: په بېلابېلو دینونو کې کوم ګډ کارونه او ارزښتونه شته؟
items.a: Most religions include prayer or worship, fasting or self-control, charity and helping the poor, special festivals, places of worship, respect for parents and elders, honesty, kindness, avoiding violence and stealing, and caring for others. These shared values help people of different faiths live together peacefully with respect.
items.e: عبادت، روزہ یا ضبطِ نفس، خیرات، تہوار، عبادت گاہیں، بڑوں کا احترام، دیانت، رحم دلی، عدم تشدد۔

items.q: Complete the chart for the Stupa built during Ashoka's empire (visual details, inferences, message).
items.q2: اشوک کے دور کے اسٹوپا کا چارٹ مکمل کریں (بصری تفصیلات، نتائج، پیغام)۔
items.q3: د اشوک د دورې سټوپا چارټ بشپړ کړئ (لیدني جزییات، پایلې، پیغام).
items.a: Visual details: a huge dome-shaped (hemispherical) brick-and-stone mound, a small square railing and umbrella on top, a stone railing and carved gateway around it, brown-red stone surrounded by green trees. Inferences: the empire was rich and organised enough to build large, lasting monuments; skilled architects and stone carvers worked for the emperor; Buddhism was important and supported by Ashoka. Message: Ashoka wanted to honour the Buddha (the stupa is believed to hold his ashes) and spread Buddhist teachings of peace across his empire.
items.e: تفصیلات: گنبد نما ٹیلہ، اوپر چھتری، جنگلہ؛ نتائج: دولت، ہنرمند کاریگر، بدھ مت کی سرپرستی؛ پیغام: بدھ کی تعظیم اور امن کا پھیلاؤ۔

items.q3: د نقشې په مرسته د کوشاني امپراتورۍ سیمې وښیاست.
items.a: Bactria and parts of Sogdiana and Ferghana (today's Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan), the Hindu Kush and Pamir mountains, Gandhara with Taxila and Peshawar (northern Pakistan), Arachosia and Gedrosia (southern Afghanistan and Balochistan), the Indus Valley and north India as far as Mathura and Saketa toward Bihar.
items.e: باختر، سغدیانہ، ہندوکش، پامیر، گندھارا (ٹیکسلا، پشاور)، اراکوزیا، گیدروسیا، وادیِ سندھ، متھرا تک شمالی ہند۔

items.q: What are Stupas?
items.q2: اسٹوپا کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: سټوپې څه دي؟
items.a: Stupas are dome-shaped Buddhist monuments built to hold relics such as the ashes of the Buddha and to honour his life and teachings. Ashoka built many stupas; the Great Stupa at Sanchi is the most famous and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
items.e: گنبد نما بدھ یادگاریں جن میں تبرکات رکھے جاتے ہیں، جیسے سانچی۔

items.q: Describe the similarities in art and architecture of Kushans and Guptas.
items.q2: کشانوں اور گپتاؤں کے فن اور فنِ تعمیر میں مماثلتیں بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د کوشانیانو او ګوپتایانو په هنر او معمارۍ کې ورته والي بیان کړئ.
items.a: Both dynasties were great patrons of art. Both produced fine religious sculpture, especially images of the Buddha; both issued beautiful gold coins showing their kings; both supported rock-cut and religious architecture (Kushan monasteries such as Takht-i-Bahi; Gupta-era cave temples and paintings such as those at Ajanta); and both mixed local Indian styles with ideas from other cultures.
items.e: دونوں سرپرست، بدھ مجسمے، سونے کے سکے، مذہبی تعمیرات اور غار، مختلف اسالیب کا امتزاج۔

items.q: Comparing: Is there any other country in the world that has a similar police state like Chandragupta's? Present your arguments in your notebooks.
items.q2: موازنہ: کیا دنیا میں کوئی اور ملک ہے جو چندر گپت کی طرح کی پولیس ریاست ہو؟ اپنے دلائل کاپیوں میں لکھیں۔
items.q3: پرتله: ایا په نړۍ کې بل داسې هېواد شته چې د چندراګوپتا په څېر پولیسي دولت ولري؟ خپل دلیلونه په کتابچو کې ولیکئ.
items.a: A "police state" is one where the government strictly controls people, forbids criticism and uses a large army or police to keep order — like Chandragupta, who made strict laws, forbade challenges to the government and kept a huge army and trained officials. In modern times, some authoritarian states (for example North Korea) are often described this way, because people cannot freely criticise the government. Most modern democracies, in contrast, protect freedom of speech and allow peaceful opposition, though they still use police to keep law and order.
items.e: Answers should give reasons and avoid unfair labels.

items.e: Shudras were the working class at the bottom of the four castes.

items.q: The Aryans were a group of nomadic tribes from:
items.q2: آریائی کس علاقے کے خانہ بدوش قبائل تھے؟ (الف) یونان (ب) فارس (ج) وسطی ایشیا (د) چین
items.q3: آریایان د کوم ځای کوچۍ قبیلې وې؟ (الف) یونان (ب) پارس (ج) منځنۍ اسیا (د) چین

items.q: Describe the social structure of Aryans.
items.q2: آریاؤں کا سماجی ڈھانچا بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د آریایانو ټولنیز جوړښت بیان کړئ.
items.a: The Aryans divided society into four castes: Brahmins (priests and teachers) at the top; Kshatriyas (kings, rulers and warriors); Vaishyas (merchants, traders, craftsmen, landowners and farmers); and Shudras (farm workers, unskilled workers and servants). Outside the caste system were the Dalits or Untouchables, who did jobs the upper castes considered unclean, such as sweeping streets and cleaning waste. The system was hereditary, so people could not change their caste. Later, Mahavira and the Buddha tried to reform it to promote equality.
items.e: چار ذاتیں — برہمن، کھشتری، ویش، شودر — اور ذات سے باہر دلت؛ موروثی نظام۔

items.q: Identify the informative parts of the Chandragupta Maurya postage stamp.
items.q2: چندر گپت موریہ کے ڈاک ٹکٹ کے معلوماتی حصے بتائیں۔
items.q3: د چندراګوپتا موریا د پوستي ټکټ معلوماتي برخې وښیاست.
items.a: The picture (the emperor seated on his throne with symbols around him), the name of the person shown (Chandragupta Maurya), the issuing country's name (India, in Hindi and English), the face value (4.00 rupees), and the perforated edges; the year of issue (2001) is also printed in small type.
items.e: تصویر، نام، ملک کا نام، قیمت (4.00)، سوراخ دار کنارے، سال۔

items.q: Was Chandragupta's rule tyrannical? Give three facts and a synthesis.
items.q2: کیا چندر گپت کی حکومت جابرانہ تھی؟ تین حقائق اور ایک ترکیب لکھیں۔
items.q3: ایا د چندراګوپتا حکومت ظالمانه و؟ درې حقایق او یو ترکیب ولیکئ.
items.a: Fact 1: He imposed strict laws, but they were fair and applied to everyone. Fact 2: People were forbidden from challenging the laws or the government, and he kept a huge army. Fact 3: He set up regional governors, a civil service that gave justice and security to merchants, and a smooth tax system, and Mauryan cities became prosperous. Synthesis: Chandragupta's rule was strict and allowed no opposition, so it had some features of tyranny, but because the laws were fair and the government brought order, justice and prosperity, it was a strong, well-organised rule rather than a cruel one.
items.e: Students may reach a different reasoned conclusion.

items.q: What evidence is there in this source that Mauryan India valued agriculture?
items.q2: اس ماخذ میں کیا ثبوت ہے کہ موریہ ہندوستان زراعت کو اہمیت دیتا تھا؟
items.q3: په دې سرچینه کې څه ثبوت شته چې موریا هند کرنې ته ارزښت ورکاوه؟
items.a: Farmers were excused from military service so they could keep farming; they could cultivate their land "undisturbed by fear"; and soldiers protected them so that ploughing went on safely even while battles were being fought nearby. This shows the government treated farming as too important to interrupt, because food and taxes on agriculture supported the empire.
items.e: کسان فوجی خدمت سے مستثنیٰ، بے خوف کاشت، جنگ کے دوران بھی فوج کی حفاظت — زراعت کو سب سے اہم سمجھا گیا۔

items.q: How did Ashoka evolve from a ruthless tyrant to a kind ruler? Give facts, inferences and a conclusion.
items.q2: اشوک بے رحم جابر سے مہربان حکمران کیسے بنا؟ حقائق، اندازے اور نتیجہ لکھیں۔
items.q3: اشوک څنګه له بې رحمه ظالم څخه مهربان واکمن شو؟ حقایق، اټکلونه او پایله ولیکئ.
items.a: Facts: early in his reign he was ambitious and fiercely aggressive and expanded the empire by bloody conquest; the widespread bloodshed shocked him; he gave up armed conquest, adopted Buddhism, carved edicts of non-violence on pillars, stopped royal hunting and animal sacrifice, protected animals and built veterinary hospitals, and focused on his subjects' welfare and justice. Inferences: seeing the suffering of war made him feel guilt and pity; Buddhist teachings of tolerance and non-violence gave him a new way to rule. Conclusion: Ashoka changed because the horror of his own wars and the influence of Buddhism made him value peace and people's welfare more than conquest.
items.e: حقائق: ابتدا میں جارح، خونریز فتوحات؛ بعد میں بدھ مت، فرامین، جانوروں کا تحفظ؛ اندازہ: جنگ کی تباہی سے ندامت؛ نتیجہ: جنگ کی ہولناکی اور بدھ مت نے اسے امن پسند بنایا۔

items.q: The capital of Maurya Empire was:
items.q2: موریہ سلطنت کا دارالحکومت تھا: (الف) پرش پور (ب) ٹیکسلا (ج) مگدھ (د) پاٹلی پتر
items.q3: د موریا امپراتورۍ پلازمېنه وه: (الف) پرشاپور (ب) ټکسیلا (ج) مګدها (د) پاټلي پوترا

items.q: When did Chandragupta establish Mauryan empire?
items.q2: چندر گپت نے موریہ سلطنت کب قائم کی؟
items.q3: چندراګوپتا د موریا امپراتوري کله جوړه کړه؟
items.a: Around 321 BCE. After Alexander's death (323 BC) he defeated the Greek troops left in the Punjab, then defeated the Nanda armies of Magadha and made himself emperor, with Pataliputra as his capital.

items.q: Explain the importance of Arthashastra for Chandragupta Mauryan.
items.q2: چندر گپت موریہ کے لیے ارتھ شاستر کی اہمیت بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د چندراګوپتا موریا لپاره د ارتهاشاستر اهمیت تشریح کړئ.
items.a: The Arthashastra, written by his advisor Chanakya Kautilya, was a Sanskrit guide on diplomacy, economic policy and military strategy. Chandragupta set up his centralized government, network of governors, civil service, army and tax system according to its principles.
items.e: مشیر کوٹلیہ کی کتاب؛ سفارت، معیشت، فوج؛ اسی کے اصولوں پر مرکزی حکومت۔

items.q: Make a list of the contributions of Ashoka as the great King.
items.q2: عظیم بادشاہ کے طور پر اشوک کی خدمات کی فہرست بنائیں۔
items.q3: د یوه لوی پاچا په توګه د اشوک ونډې لېست کړئ.
items.a: 1) Expanded the Mauryan Empire over almost the whole Subcontinent. 2) Gave up war after the bloodshed of conquest and adopted peaceful "conquest by religion". 3) Spread Buddhism beyond the empire by sending missionaries to Southeast Asia. 4) Focused on the welfare and prosperity of his subjects, with direct tax collection on agriculture and justice for the people. 5) Carved edicts of non-violence on rocks and pillars along trade routes and pilgrim sites. 6) Protected wildlife, banned royal hunting and animal sacrifice, and built free veterinary hospitals. 7) Encouraged art and architecture — Ashoka's pillars and stupas such as Sanchi.
items.e: توسیع، جنگ کا ترک، بدھ مت کی تبلیغ، رعایا کی بہبود، فرامین، جنگلی حیات کا تحفظ، ستون اور اسٹوپا۔

items.q: What was Ashoka's strategy for promoting peace in his empire?
items.q2: اپنی سلطنت میں امن کو فروغ دینے کے لیے اشوک کی حکمتِ عملی کیا تھی؟
items.q3: په خپله امپراتورۍ کې د سولې د هڅولو لپاره د اشوک ستراتیژي څه وه؟
items.a: He gave up armed conquest and followed "conquest by religion" based on Buddhist ideals of tolerance, non-violence and good behaviour; he carved edicts on rocks and pillars to teach these values; he cared for his subjects' welfare and gave them justice; he practised non-violence towards animals; and he sent missionaries to spread Buddhist teachings of peace.
items.e: جنگ ترک، رواداری و عدم تشدد، فرامین، رعایا کی بہبود و انصاف، مبلغین۔

items.q: Compare Kanishka and Ashoka: religions, works for development, taxes and attitude towards people.
items.q2: کنشک اور اشوک کا موازنہ کریں: مذاہب، ترقیاتی کام، ٹیکس اور لوگوں سے رویّہ۔
items.q3: کنیشکا او اشوک پرتله کړئ: دینونه، پرمختیايي کارونه، مالیات او له خلکو سره چلند.
items.a: Religions — Kanishka: a Buddhist who promoted Buddhism, while his empire also followed Zoroastrian and Greek cults; Ashoka: embraced Buddhism and spread it through missionaries and edicts. Works for development — Kanishka: expanded trade on the Silk Road, made friendly links with Rome and China, supported Gandhara art and Sanskrit, built monasteries; Ashoka: built stupas, pillars and veterinary hospitals and protected wildlife. Taxes — Kanishka: grew rich from Silk Road trade and issued gold coins (the book gives no detail); Ashoka: collected taxes directly on agriculture. Attitude towards people — Kanishka: known for military and political success with tolerance of many cultures; Ashoka: after Kalinga, focused on welfare, justice, non-violence and kindness to all.

items.q: Choose an object or image that symbolizes how three rulers of this chapter exercised power, with captions.
items.q2: اس باب کے تین حکمرانوں کی طاقت کی علامت والی اشیا اور عنوانات منتخب کریں۔
items.q3: د دې څپرکي د درېیو واکمنانو د واک نښې او سرلیکونه غوره کړئ.
items.a: Chandragupta Maurya — a sword or army: "He ruled with a huge army and strict laws to keep order in a vast empire." Ashoka — a stone pillar with an edict: "After Kalinga he ruled by teaching non-violence and caring for his people." Kanishka — a gold coin: "His coins show the wealth and trade of the Kushan Empire and his support for Buddhism."
items.e: Students may choose other rulers and symbols.

items.q: Kushan Empire's greatest emperor was:
items.q2: کشان سلطنت کا عظیم ترین شہنشاہ تھا: (الف) کنشک (ب) کدفیسس (ج) ورن (د) کوٹلیہ
items.q3: د کوشاني امپراتورۍ تر ټولو لوی امپراتور و: (الف) کنیشکا (ب) کدفیسس (ج) ورونا (د) کوټلیا

items.q: What were the links between Gandhara art and Kushan?
items.q2: گندھارا فن اور کشانوں کے درمیان کیا تعلق تھا؟
items.q3: د ګندهارا هنر او کوشانیانو ترمنځ څه اړیکه وه؟
items.a: The Kushans ruled Gandhara from about 75 CE, and their period is called the Golden Period of Gandhara. Kanishka, a Buddhist, supported Gandhara art — a blend of Greco-Roman and Indian (Buddhist) styles seen in Buddha sculptures and on Kushan coins — and his capital Purushapur (Peshawar) was in Gandhara.
items.e: کشانوں کا گندھارا پر راج، سنہری دور، کنشک کی سرپرستی، یونانی-ہندوستانی امتزاج۔

items.q: Who was Kanishka?
items.q2: کنشک کون تھا؟
items.q3: کنیشکا څوک و؟
items.a: Kanishka was the greatest emperor of the Kushan Empire. His empire stretched from Bihar to the Indus Valley, with its capital at Purushapur near Peshawar. A follower of Buddhism, he promoted its teachings, supported Gandhara art and the Silk Road, and made the Kushans one of the four great powers of Eurasia.
items.e: کشان سلطنت کا عظیم ترین شہنشاہ، دارالحکومت پروش پور، بدھ مت کا حامی۔

items.q: Describe the importance of Ajanta and Ellora caves from a historical view point.
items.q2: تاریخی نقطۂ نظر سے اجنتا اور ایلورا کے غاروں کی اہمیت بیان کریں۔
items.q3: له تاریخي لید څخه د اجنتا او ایلورا د سمڅو اهمیت بیان کړئ.
items.a: They are masterpieces of rock-cut art and UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Ajanta's 29 Buddhist caves (2nd century BC – 6th century AD) and Ellora's 34 Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves (6th – 11th centuries AD) show how religions lived side by side; their sculptures, murals and paintings tell us about Buddhist life, beliefs and values; they served as monasteries, worship halls and resting places for monks, merchants and pilgrims; and the funding by various emperors shows royal support for religion and art.
items.e: عالمی ورثہ؛ مذاہب کا ہم آہنگ وجود؛ فن سے عقائد کا علم؛ خانقاہیں اور آرام گاہیں؛ شاہی سرپرستی۔

items.q: Make a list of the Prophets (علیہم السلام) whose names appear in the Quran.
items.q2: ان انبیاء علیہم السلام کی فہرست بنائیں جن کے نام قرآن میں آئے ہیں۔
items.q3: د هغو پیغمبرانو (علیهم السلام) لېست جوړ کړئ چې نومونه یې په قرآن کې راغلي.
items.a: Twenty-five prophets are named in the Quran: Adam, Idrees, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Yousuf, Ayyub, Shoaib, Musa, Haroon, Dhul-Kifl, Dawood, Sulaiman, Ilyas, Al-Yasa, Younus, Zakariya, Yahya, Esa and Muhammad (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم).
items.e: قرآن میں 25 انبیاء کے نام: آدم، ادریس، نوح، ہود، صالح، ابراہیم، لوط، اسماعیل، اسحاق، یعقوب، یوسف، ایوب، شعیب، موسیٰ، ہارون، ذوالکفل، داؤد، سلیمان، الیاس، الیسع، یونس، زکریا، یحییٰ، عیسیٰ اور محمد ﷺ۔

items.q: Give examples of how peace and co-existence were practised in Madinah and how we can practise them in daily life.
items.q2: مدینہ میں امن اور بقائے باہمی کی مثالیں دیں اور بتائیں کہ ہم روزمرہ زندگی میں ان پر کیسے عمل کر سکتے ہیں۔
items.q3: په مدینه کې د سولې او ګډ ژوند بېلګې ورکړئ او ووایاست چې موږ یې په ورځني ژوند کې څنګه عملي کولای شو.
items.a: In Madinah: the Charter let Muslims, Jews and others live together with equal rights and freedom of religion; the brotherhood of Ansaar and Muhajireen shared homes and work; even in war, children, the old and those seeking protection were not harmed. In daily life: respect neighbours of other faiths, share with those in need, solve disputes by talking rather than fighting, follow the law, and avoid harming public property and the environment.
items.e: میثاق، مواخات، جنگ میں بھی رحم؛ روزمرہ: پڑوسیوں کا احترام، مدد، بات چیت سے حل، قانون کی پابندی۔

items.q: How can good governance be ensured through declaration of assets?
items.q2: اثاثوں کے اعلان سے اچھی حکمرانی کیسے یقینی بنائی جا سکتی ہے؟
items.q3: د شتمنۍ په اعلان ښه حکومتولي څنګه تضمینېږي؟
items.a: When officials declare what they own on taking office (as under Hazrat Umar رضی اللہ عنہ), any unusual increase in their wealth can be noticed and questioned. This discourages bribery and misuse of public money, makes officials accountable, and builds people's trust in the government. Today, Pakistan's members of parliament and senior officers must also file asset declarations.
items.e: عہدہ سنبھالتے وقت اثاثوں کا اعلان؛ غیر معمولی اضافہ پر جواب طلبی؛ رشوت کی روک تھام، احتساب اور اعتماد۔

items.q: Why is it important for a ruler to check social evils? What is the benefit of showing a personal example?
items.q2: حکمران کے لیے سماجی برائیوں کی روک تھام کیوں ضروری ہے؟ ذاتی مثال کا کیا فائدہ ہے؟
items.q3: واکمن ته د ټولنیزو بدیو مخنیوی ولې مهم دی؟ د شخصي بېلګې ګټه څه ده؟
items.a: Social evils such as corruption, injustice, cheating and violence weaken a society, cause conflict and make people lose trust in the state, so a ruler must stop them to keep peace and welfare. When a ruler lives honestly and simply himself (like the pious caliphs), people respect and copy him, officials are afraid to misuse power, and his orders are obeyed willingly.
items.e: برائیاں معاشرے کو کمزور کرتی ہیں؛ حکمران کی ذاتی مثال سے لوگ پیروی کرتے اور افسر بدعنوانی سے ڈرتے ہیں۔

items.q: What lessons can be drawn from State of Madinah for a prosperous Pakistan?
items.q2: خوشحال پاکستان کے لیے ریاستِ مدینہ سے کیا اسباق حاصل کیے جا سکتے ہیں؟
items.q3: د سوکاله پاکستان لپاره د مدینې له دولت څه درسونه اخیستل کېدای شي؟
items.a: Rule of law and equal justice for rich and poor; honest, simple and accountable leaders (asset declaration, as under Hazrat Umar); consultation (Shura) in decisions; care for the poor through Zakat and welfare (stipends for mothers and the elderly); brotherhood and unity among people of different regions and ethnic groups, like the Ansaar and Muhajireen; protection and freedom for minorities; and peaceful solutions to disputes.
items.e: قانون کی بالادستی، دیانت دار قیادت، شوریٰ، زکوٰۃ و فلاح، اخوت، اقلیتوں کا تحفظ، پرامن حل۔

items.q: Comparing: Explain the similarities between the periods of Khulafa e Rashideen (رضی اللہ عنہم).
items.q2: موازنہ: خلفائے راشدین رضی اللہ عنہم کے ادوار کی مماثلتیں بیان کریں۔
items.q3: پرتله: د خلفای راشدینو (رضی الله عنهم) د دورو ورته والي تشریح کړئ.
items.a: All four caliphs: governed according to the Quran and Sunnah; used consultation (Shura); lived simple lives and did not misuse public money; gave equal justice to everyone, including non-Muslims, with independent Qazis; appointed governors and Aamils for provinces and districts; cared for the poor; worked to spread Islam; and were chosen with the agreement of the leading companions.
items.e: قرآن و سنت، شوریٰ، سادگی، انصاف، صوبائی انتظام، غریبوں کی فلاح، اشاعتِ اسلام۔

items.q: Keeping in view Charter of Madinah, which steps should be taken today to make this world a peaceful place.
items.q2: میثاقِ مدینہ کو مدِنظر رکھتے ہوئے آج دنیا کو پرامن بنانے کے لیے کون سے اقدامات کیے جائیں؟
items.q3: د مدینې میثاق په پام کې نیولو سره، نن د نړۍ د سوله ییزې کولو لپاره کوم ګامونه پورته شي؟
items.a: Make written agreements that give all communities equal rights; respect freedom of religion; solve disputes through dialogue rather than war; cooperate against common threats such as terrorism, poverty and climate change; protect minorities, women and children; and follow the rule of law in international relations (e.g. through the United Nations).
items.e: برابر حقوق کے معاہدے، مذہبی آزادی، مکالمہ، مشترکہ خطرات کے خلاف تعاون، اقلیتوں کا تحفظ، بین الاقوامی قانون۔

items.q: Using the atlas, identify the location of the Islamic World during the reign of Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ).
items.q2: اٹلس کی مدد سے حضرت علی رضی اللہ عنہ کے دور میں اسلامی دنیا کا محلِ وقوع بتائیں۔
items.q3: د اټلس په مرسته د حضرت علي (رضی الله عنه) په دوره کې د اسلامي نړۍ موقعیت وښیاست.
items.a: By 656–661 AD the Islamic world covered the Arabian Peninsula, Iraq, Syria and Palestine, Egypt and Libya in North Africa, and Persia (Iran) to the borders of Afghanistan and Central Asia, with parts of Armenia and Azerbaijan — lands around the Red Sea, the Persian Gulf and the eastern Mediterranean, in today's Middle East. The capital moved from Madinah to Kufa in Iraq.
items.e: جزیرہ نمائے عرب، عراق، شام، فلسطین، مصر، لیبیا، ایران؛ دارالحکومت کوفہ۔

items.q: Give some examples of the hardships that Hazrat Muhammad Rasool Allah Khatam-un-Nabiyeen (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) faced at the advent of Islam.
items.q2: اسلام کے آغاز میں حضرت محمد رسول اللہ خاتم النبیین ﷺ کو پیش آنے والی چند مشکلات کی مثالیں دیں۔
items.q3: د اسلام په پیل کې حضرت محمد رسول الله خاتم النبیین ﷺ ته د پېښو شوو سختیو بېلګې ورکړئ.
items.a: The elite of Makkah opposed the message because they did not want to lose their superiority; Muslims suffered physical beating; they faced a social and economic boycott and other atrocities; finally, in 622 AD, the Muslims had to leave their homes and migrate to Madinah.
items.e: مکہ کے اشرافیہ کی مخالفت، جسمانی تشدد، سماجی و معاشی بائیکاٹ، ہجرت پر مجبوری۔

items.q: What, in your view, was the biggest factor that changed Arabian society?
items.q2: آپ کے خیال میں عرب معاشرے کو بدلنے والا سب سے بڑا عامل کیا تھا؟
items.q3: ستاسو په اند عربي ټولنه تر ټولو لوی کوم لامل بدله کړه؟
items.a: Sample view: the personal example and leadership of Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم). People trusted him as Sadiq and Amin; he practised what he taught — equality, justice, honesty and care for the poor — so people followed his example, and the message of equality, women's rights and the system of Zakat became part of daily life.
items.e: Students may choose another factor from the text with reasons.
